key: COMP.DIG.L01.01|What does Moshe do first? Look at the screen, sit up straight, or put his hands down?
how: Watch how Moshe gets ready. First he sits up straight. Then he puts his two hands on the table. Then he looks at the screen. Now he is ready to learn!

key: COMP.DIG.L01.01|Your hands are sticky from cake. What do you do first? Wipe them on the keys, wash your hands, or start the computer?
COMP.DIG.L01.01|Put Moshe's steps in order. The cards say: Look at the screen, Sit up straight, Put two hands on the table.
COMP.DIG.L01.01|Abba is using the computer for his work. What should you do? Wait and ask first, close the lid, or press the keys?
COMP.DIG.L01.01|How do you sit at the computer? Lie on the floor, sit up straight, or stand on the chair?
COMP.DIG.L01.02|What does Dovid do first? Swipe the screen, find it with his eyes, or lift his finger fast?
how: Watch how Dovid picks the apple picture. He finds the apple with his eyes. He puts one finger right on it. He lifts his finger fast. Tap! The apple is picked.

key: COMP.DIG.L01.02|You want the lion picture. What do you do? Swipe away, tap the lion, or tap the bird?

COMP.DIG.L01.02|Where do you tap and swipe? On the juice box, on the chair, or on the screen?
how: The skill underneath: Hello, Computer (Computing Level 1). You tap and swipe on the screen, the part that shows pictures.

how: The keys have letters on them, just like the letters you know! When you find the letters of your name, the computer can write your name. Let us find letters, the long space bar and the backspace key.

key: COMP.TYPE.L01.01|Moshe's name starts with M. Which letter does he look for? M, O, or S?
how: A simpler step: find just one letter, the first letter of your name. Say it, then look for it.

key: COMP.DIG.L02.01|After you turn it on, how do you get into your lessons? Sign in with your own code, or press every key?
COMP.DIG.L02.01|Your hands are sticky from lunch. What should you do before you use the Chromebook? Wash your hands, or use it anyway?
COMP.DIG.L02.01|Look at the pictures. Which one is a computer? The computer, or the ball?
how: The skill underneath: this is a first skill (Start). Before any computer, you learn to look carefully and point at things.

key: COMP.PROG.L02.01|What comes first? Socks, or shoes?
how: Steps must be in the right order. To put on shoes: first socks, then shoes, then tie the laces.

key: COMP.PROG.L02.01|Which step is more exact? Walk two steps forward, or walk somewhere?
how: Each step must be exact. "Walk" is not enough. "Walk two steps forward" tells the robot exactly what to do.

key: COMP.PROG.L02.01|Robot Ari wants to wash his hands. What comes first? Turn on the water, or dry your hands?
COMP.PROG.L02.01|Which step is exact? Take one big step to the right, or go over there?
COMP.PROG.L02.01|Tell the robot how to fill a cup with water. Tap the steps in order.
COMP.PROG.L02.01|The robot got stuck. The plan was: put on shoes, put on socks. What went wrong? The steps are in the wrong order, or the robot is tired?
COMP.PROG.L02.01|Robot Dov wants to eat an apple. What comes first? Say the bracha, or eat the apple?
COMP.PROG.L02.01|Tell the robot how to go into the classroom. Tap the steps in order.
COMP.PROG.L02.01|What comes first? Open the book, or read the page?
COMP.PROG.L02.01|Which step is exact? Turn left, or turn?
COMP.PROG.L02.01|Tell the robot how to plant a seed. Tap the steps in order.
COMP.PROG.L02.01|Your friend says: take one step. How many steps do you take? One, or three?
how: A new way: play robot. A friend gives you one step at a time, and you do only that step, nothing more.

key: COMP.PROG.L02.01|What comes first? Open the box, or take out the toy?
how: A simpler step: just two steps. Which one has to happen before the other?

key: COMP.PROG.L02.01|Rebbi says: clap, then stand up. What do you do first? Clap, or stand up?
how: The skill underneath: this is a first skill (Start). It starts with listening carefully and doing exactly what you hear, in order.

key: COMP.DIG.L02.02|You want to choose the red button. What do you do? Point at it and click, or close the lid?
COMP.DIG.L02.02|Put the steps of drag and drop in order. Tap them in order.
COMP.DIG.L02.02|You clicked the wrong thing by mistake. What can you do? Calmly click the right one, or bang the keyboard?
COMP.DIG.L02.02|Point at the star and press once. What did you do? A click, or a drag?
how: A simpler step: only click. Point at one thing and press once.

key: COMP.TYPE.L02.01|Your thumbs rest on one long key at the bottom. Which key? The space bar, or the power button?
COMP.TYPE.L02.01|Put the left-hand home keys in order, from your little finger to your pointer finger.
COMP.TYPE.L02.01|What do you use to move the pointer? The trackpad, or the home row?
how: The skill underneath: Click, Drag, Drop (Computing Level 2). You already move the pointer with one finger. Now all your fingers learn their places on the keys.

key: COMP.PROG.L02.02|How many right arrows reach the apple? Two, or three?
how: Count the squares first. One arrow moves one square. One empty square and then the apple means two moves.

key: COMP.PROG.L02.02|Which blocks reach the apple? Two right arrows then one up arrow, or one up arrow only?
how: Paths can turn. Read the grid like a map: the robot is here, the apple is there. Go across first, then up.

key: COMP.PROG.L02.02|Which blocks reach the apple? Four right arrows, or three right arrows?
COMP.PROG.L02.02|The apple is above the robot. Which blocks reach it? Two up arrows, or two right arrows?
COMP.PROG.L02.02|The apple is to the left. Which blocks reach it? Two left arrows, or two right arrows?
COMP.PROG.L02.02|A wall 🧱 is in the way. Snap the blocks in order to reach the apple, then pick it up.
COMP.PROG.L02.02|A bigger grid. Which blocks reach the apple? Two up arrows then one right arrow, or one up arrow only?
COMP.PROG.L02.02|Which blocks reach the apple? Three right arrows, or four right arrows?
COMP.PROG.L02.02|Which blocks reach the apple? Three left arrows, or three right arrows?
COMP.PROG.L02.02|Which block reaches the apple? One left arrow, or one up arrow?
COMP.PROG.L02.02|Walk your finger one square to the right. Where does it land? On the empty square, or on the apple?
how: A new way: walk it with your finger. Put your finger on the robot. Move it one square for each arrow, and see where it lands.

key: COMP.PROG.L02.02|Which one block reaches the apple? One right arrow, or one left arrow?
how: A simpler step: one arrow, one square. The apple is right next to the robot.

key: COMP.DIG.L02.03|Your best friend asks for your code. What do you say? No, it is private, or here it is?
how: Never tell your password to a friend, even a best friend. A friend could make a mistake with your work by accident.

key: COMP.DIG.L02.03|Someone saw your code. Who do you tell? Your rebbe, or nobody?
how: If someone sees your password, tell your rebbe. He can help you get a new one.

key: COMP.DIG.L02.03|Where should your password stay? In your head, or on a sign on your desk?
COMP.DIG.L02.03|Who may know your password? You and your rebbe, or the whole class?
COMP.DIG.L02.03|A message on the screen asks for your code, and you do not know who sent it. What do you do? Ask your rebbe first, or type it in?
COMP.DIG.L02.03|You are done for the day. What should you do so nobody uses your account? Sign out, or leave it open?
COMP.DIG.L02.03|Why is your password like the key to your house? It keeps others out, or it opens every door in town?
COMP.DIG.L02.03|Zeidy has a secret code for his bank card. Should he tell it to a stranger on the phone? No, or yes?
COMP.DIG.L02.03|Is your password a secret? Yes, or no?
COMP.DIG.L02.03|A boy in your class asks for your code to play a game. What do you do? Keep it private, or tell him?
COMP.DIG.L02.03|You finish your lesson and walk away. What do you do first? Sign out, or turn up the sound?
COMP.DIG.L02.03|Do you share your toothbrush? No, or yes?
how: A new way: your password is like a toothbrush. It is only for you, and you never share it.

key: COMP.DIG.L02.03|Whose password is it? Mine, or everyone's?
how: A simpler step: one rule. My password stays mine.

key: COMP.TYPE.L03.01|Which letter is on the top row? R, or N?
COMP.TYPE.L03.01|Which letter is on the bottom row? M, or O?
COMP.TYPE.L03.01|Your left little finger rests on A. Which top key does it reach? Q, or P?
COMP.TYPE.L03.01|Your right pointer finger rests on J. Which bottom key does it reach? M, or Z?
COMP.TYPE.L03.01|Put the first top-row letters in order, from left to right.
COMP.TYPE.L03.01|Which letter is on the top row? U, or B?
COMP.TYPE.L03.01|Your left ring finger rests on S. Which bottom key does it reach? X, or N?
COMP.TYPE.L03.01|Your elevator finger is on D. It goes up one floor. Which key? E, or Z?
how: A new way: each finger is a little elevator. It goes up one floor to the top row, down one floor to the bottom row, and always comes back to its home floor.

key: COMP.PROG.L03.01|The robot should reach the apple, but it goes up. Which step is the bug? The up arrow, or the right arrow?
how: A bug is a mistake in a program. When the robot goes the wrong way, a programmer does not get upset. He reads the program one step at a time, finds the wrong step, and fixes it. Finding bugs is called debugging, and every programmer does it every day!
pic: 🤖⬜🍎\nProgram: ➡️ ⬆️

key: COMP.PROG.L03.01|Walk it with your finger. Which arrow is wrong? The left arrow, or the first right arrow?
how: To find a bug, walk the program with your finger, one arrow at a time. Stop at the first arrow that goes the wrong way.
pic: 🤖⬜⬜🍎\nProgram: ➡️ ⬅️ ➡️

key: COMP.PROG.L03.01|How do you fix this program? Change the up arrow to a right arrow, or start over from nothing?
how: To fix a bug, change only the wrong step. Keep the good steps.
pic: 🤖⬜⬜🍎\nProgram: ➡️ ➡️ ⬆️

pic: 🤖⬜🍎⬜\nProgram: ➡️ ➡️ ➡️

key: COMP.PROG.L03.01|Your program has a bug. What is the best first step? Walk it slowly with your finger, or delete everything?
COMP.PROG.L03.01|Steps for washing hands: dry hands, soap, rinse. What is the bug? Dry hands is in the wrong place, or soap is missing?
COMP.PROG.L03.01|Which arrow is the bug? The down arrow, or the right arrow?
pic: 🤖⬜🍎\nProgram: ⬇️ ➡️

key: COMP.PROG.L03.01|How do you fix it? Change the down arrow to an up arrow, or add a left arrow?
pic: ⬜🍎\n🤖⬜\nProgram: ➡️ ⬇️

key: COMP.PROG.L03.01|What is a bug in a program? A mistake in the steps, or a real insect in the computer?
COMP.PROG.L03.01|Which step moves the robot away? The left arrow, or a right arrow?
how: A new way: be a detective. Check each step like a clue: does this arrow move the robot closer to the apple? The first step that moves it away is the bug.
pic: 🤖⬜🍎\nProgram: ⬅️ ➡️ ➡️

key: COMP.PROG.L03.01|Is this one arrow right, or is it a bug? It is a bug, or it is right?
how: A simpler step: a program with just one arrow. Does it point toward the apple?
pic: 🍎🤖\nProgram: ➡️

key: COMP.PROG.L03.01|Which one arrow reaches the apple? Right, or up?
how: The skill underneath: Robot Paths (Computing Level 2). Each arrow moves the robot one square. Know the path first, then check the program.

key: COMP.PROG.L03.02|Right, right, right, right. Which repeat block does the same thing? Repeat 4 times right, or repeat 2 times right?
how: When a program says the same thing again and again, like right, right, right, right, there is a shortcut: a repeat block. Repeat 4 times: right. It does the same job with fewer blocks, and it is easier to read and to fix. Real programmers use repeat all the time!

key: COMP.PROG.L03.02|How many times does up repeat? 3, or 4?
how: To build a repeat block, count how many times the same step comes in a row. That number goes in the block.

key: COMP.PROG.L03.02|Clap, stomp, clap, stomp, clap, stomp. Which block fits? Repeat 3 times clap stomp, or repeat 6 times clap?
how: A repeat can hold more than one step. Clap, stomp, clap, stomp, clap, stomp is: repeat 3 times clap, stomp.

key: COMP.PROG.L03.02|Which repeat block reaches the apple? Repeat 5 times right, or repeat 4 times right?
COMP.PROG.L03.02|Down, down. Which repeat block matches? Repeat 2 times down, or repeat 2 times up?
COMP.PROG.L03.02|Which program is shorter to read? Repeat 10 times hop, or hop written 10 times?
COMP.PROG.L03.02|Shimon draws a star, a star and a star. Which block fits? Repeat 3 times draw a star, or repeat 1 time draw a star?
COMP.PROG.L03.02|Zeidy walks up 12 steps to his apartment. Which repeat block describes it? Repeat 12 times step up, or repeat 2 times step up?
COMP.PROG.L03.02|Which repeat block matches? Repeat 6 times right, or repeat 5 times right?
COMP.PROG.L03.02|Jump, turn, jump, turn. Which block fits? Repeat 2 times jump turn, or repeat 4 times jump?
COMP.PROG.L03.02|A chorus is sung 3 times. How do you write it? Once, with repeat 3 times, or 3 times out in full?
how: A new way: think of a song with a chorus. You do not write the chorus out every time. You write it once and say: sing it 3 times.

key: COMP.PROG.L03.02|How many left arrows? 2, or 3?
how: A simpler step: just count. Count the same arrows in a row.

key: COMP.PROG.L03.02|Which steps are the same? The two right arrows, or the right and the up?
how: The skill underneath: Bug Hunt (Computing Level 3). Read a program one step at a time. Then you can see which steps are the same.
pic: Program: ➡️ ➡️ ⬆️

key: COMP.DIG.L03.01|What do you do so the computer keeps your work? Save it, or close it without saving?
how: When you make something on a computer, you save it as a file, like a page that the computer keeps. Files go in folders, like papers in a binder. Give each file a clear name, so you can find it tomorrow. Saving and naming means your work is never lost!

key: COMP.DIG.L03.01|Which file name is best for a story about Chanukah? Chanukah story, or untitled?
how: A good file name tells what is inside. Chanukah story is better than untitled.

key: COMP.DIG.L03.01|Where does your reading story go? In the Reading folder, or in the Math folder?
how: Folders hold files that go together. Put all your math work in a Math folder.
pic: 📁 Math\n📁 Reading

key: COMP.DIG.L03.01|You finished a drawing. What should you do first? Save it, or turn off the computer?
COMP.DIG.L03.01|Which name is best for a picture of your sukkah? My sukkah picture, or abc123?
COMP.DIG.L03.01|Where does a page about plants go? In the Science folder, or in the Math folder?
pic: 📁 Math\n📁 Reading\n📁 Science

key: COMP.DIG.L03.01|Put the steps in order to find yesterday's work.
COMP.DIG.L03.01|You cannot find your file. What is a smart way to look? Search for its name, or make it all over again?
COMP.DIG.L03.01|Abba keeps his bills in a box marked Bills and his letters in a box marked Letters. What are the boxes like? Folders, or files?
COMP.DIG.L03.01|Which file name tells what is inside? Parsha report Noach, or file 7?
COMP.DIG.L03.01|What happens if you close your work without saving? It may be lost, or it is always kept?
COMP.DIG.L03.01|In the cabinet idea, what is a drawer? A folder, or a file?
how: A new way: the computer is a cabinet. Folders are drawers. Files are the papers inside.

key: COMP.DIG.L03.01|What comes first? Save, or close?
how: A simpler step: just one rule. Save before you close.

key: COMP.DIG.L03.01|How do you move a file into a folder? Drag it and drop it, or shake the mouse?
how: The skill underneath: Click, Drag, Drop (Computing Level 2). You open a folder with a click, and you can drag a file into a folder.

key: COMP.DIG.L03.02|Which one is software? A game app, or the screen?
how: Software is the programs. You cannot hold software in your hand. You see it on the screen.

key: COMP.DIG.L03.02|Which one is hardware? The trackpad, or a reading lesson?
COMP.DIG.L03.02|Which one is software? A typing game, or the power button?
COMP.DIG.L03.02|Can you touch software with your hand? No, or yes?
COMP.DIG.L03.02|Put the restart steps in order.
COMP.DIG.L03.02|You restarted, and it is still stuck. What now? Tell your rebbe, or keep pressing every key?
COMP.DIG.L03.02|A calculator has buttons and a program that adds numbers. Which part is the software? The program that adds, or the buttons?
COMP.DIG.L03.02|Which one is hardware? The screen, or a math lesson?
COMP.DIG.L03.02|Which one is software? A drawing app, or the keyboard?
COMP.DIG.L03.02|What is the first thing to try when a program freezes? Restart, or throw it away?
COMP.DIG.L03.02|In the person idea, what is software like? The thoughts, or the body?
how: A new way: a computer is like a person. Hardware is the body. Software is the thoughts that tell the body what to do.

key: COMP.DIG.L03.02|Can you touch the trackpad? Yes, so it is hardware, or no, so it is software?
how: A simpler step: the touch test. If you can touch it, it is hardware.

key: COMP.DIG.L03.03|Look at the chart. How many boys like apples? 4, or 2?
how: Data is information we collect, like which fruit each boy likes. When we sort it into groups and count each group, we can answer questions fast. A picture chart shows each group in its own row. Computers help us sort and count data, so let's learn how!
pic: Apples: 🍎🍎🍎🍎\nBananas: 🍌🍌\nGrapes: 🍇🍇🍇

key: COMP.DIG.L03.03|Which fruit do the most boys like? Apples, or bananas?
how: To compare, count each row. The row with the most pictures is the favorite.
pic: Apples: 🍎🍎🍎🍎\nBananas: 🍌🍌\nGrapes: 🍇🍇🍇

key: COMP.DIG.L03.03|Where does a red ball go? In the red group, or in the blue group?
how: To sort, put each thing in the group where it belongs. Red things go in the red group, blue things in the blue group.

key: COMP.DIG.L03.03|How many boys like grapes? 3, or 4?

key: COMP.DIG.L03.03|Why do we sort data into groups? So we can count and compare, or so it looks messy?
COMP.DIG.L03.03|How many cars go in the car bin? 3, or 2?
how: A new way: sort like a cleanup. All the bears go in the bear bin, all the cars in the car bin. Then count each bin.
pic: Toys: 🧸 🚗 🧸 🚗 🚗

key: COMP.DIG.L03.03|Touch and count the bananas. 2, or 3?
how: A simpler step: count one row only. Touch each picture and say a number.
pic: Bananas: 🍌🍌

key: COMP.DIG.L03.03|Where does a math sheet go? The Math folder, or the Reading folder?
how: The skill underneath: Files and Folders (Computing Level 3). Sorting data is like putting files in the right folders: each thing goes in its group.
pic: 📁 Math\n📁 Reading

key: COMP.DIG.L03.04|A box says you won a prize. What do you do? Stop and ask a grown-up, or click it fast?
how: Sometimes a box pops up on the screen with flashing words like YOU WON or CLICK HERE. These are often tricks that try to make you click. A smart computer kid stops, does not click, and asks a grown-up first. That keeps you and the computer safe!
pic: ⚠️ YOU WON A PRIZE! CLICK HERE!

key: COMP.DIG.L03.04|Which message is probably a trick? Free game, click now, or save your work?
how: Trick buttons often use flashing colors, big promises, or words like FREE, WIN or HURRY.

key: COMP.DIG.L03.04|A box says your computer is broken and to click to fix it. Who do you tell? Your rebbe, or nobody?
how: Some pop-ups say your computer is broken or has a virus. That is a trick too. Do not click. Tell your rebbe.
pic: ⚠️ YOUR COMPUTER IS BROKEN! CLICK TO FIX!

key: COMP.DIG.L03.04|A button flashes red and yellow and says HURRY. What should you do? Do not click and ask first, or click it right away?
COMP.DIG.L03.04|Which one is safe to click in your lesson? The Next button in your lesson, or a flashing prize box?

how: The skill underneath: My Password Is Mine (Computing Level 2). Never give your sign-in code to a pop-up or a stranger.

key: COMP.TYPE.L04.01|Which finger types the period at the end of a sentence? The right ring finger, the left thumb, or the right pointer finger?
how: Between words, your thumb taps the space bar one time. At the end of the sentence, the right ring finger reaches down from L to the period key.
pic: L\n.

key: COMP.TYPE.L04.01|How many spaces go between two words? One, two, or none?

COMP.TYPE.L04.01|In the train idea, what is the caboose at the end? The period, the capital letter, or a space?
how: A new way: a sentence is like a train. The capital letter is the engine in front, the words are the cars with a small gap between each, and the period is the caboose at the end.

key: COMP.TYPE.L04.01|Avi types: my sukkah is big. Which letter needs Shift? The m, the s, or the b?
how: A simpler step: just the start. Every sentence starts with a capital, so hold Shift for the very first letter.
pic: my sukkah is big.

key: COMP.TYPE.L04.01|Your right pointer finger types U. Which home key does it reach up from? J, F, or K?
how: The skill underneath: Top Row, Bottom Row (Computing Level 3). Every letter in a sentence comes from a finger that reaches up or down from home and comes back.

key: COMP.PROG.L04.01|What is the first thing to do with a big, hard job? Break it into small steps, give up, or do it all at once?
how: A big job can feel too hard, until you break it down. Programmers split a big problem into small steps, then solve one small step at a time. Building a whole game? Cleaning a whole room? Break it down, and every big job turns into a list of easy ones!

key: COMP.PROG.L04.01|Which one is a part of setting the Shabbos table? Putting out the cups, riding a bike, or doing homework?
how: To break a job down, ask: what are its parts? Setting the Shabbos table has parts: the tablecloth, the plates, the cups and the challah cover.

key: COMP.PROG.L04.01|Which goes on first when setting the table? The tablecloth, the plates, or the challah cover?
how: Small steps need a good order. The tablecloth goes on before the plates, or the plates would end up under it!

key: COMP.PROG.L04.01|Moshe wants to make a birthday card on the computer. Which is a small step of that job? Type the words, wash the car, or go to sleep?

COMP.PROG.L04.01|Chaim must write a report about his town. Which is a good first small step? Pick three facts to write about, write it all in one minute, or print it first?
COMP.PROG.L04.01|How do you eat a big watermelon? One slice at a time, all in one bite, or not at all?
how: A new way: eating a big watermelon. You cannot eat it in one bite, so you cut it into slices and eat one slice at a time.

key: COMP.PROG.L04.01|Which is a part of getting ready for yeshiva? Eating breakfast, or going to sleep?
how: A simpler step: just name a part. Getting ready for yeshiva has parts, like getting dressed and eating breakfast.

key: COMP.PROG.L04.01|Hop, hop, hop, hop. Which repeat block fits? Repeat 4 times hop, or repeat 3 times hop?
how: The skill underneath: Do It Again (Computing Level 3). When you break a job down, some small steps repeat, and a repeat block can do them for you.

key: COMP.PROG.L04.02|Look at the program. What makes these steps run? Clicking the green flag, pressing space, or nothing?
how: An event block always sits on top, with the steps under it. When the green flag is clicked, the steps under that block run.

key: COMP.PROG.L04.02|Look at the program. Mendy presses the left arrow. What happens? The player moves left, the player moves right, or the game ends?
how: A program can have many events. Each one waits for its own thing. When the right arrow is pressed, the player moves right.
pic: When right arrow pressed → move right 1\nWhen left arrow pressed → move left 1

key: COMP.PROG.L04.02|Why do games use events? So they answer what the player does, so they never change, or so the screen is bigger?
COMP.PROG.L04.02|In the switch idea, what is the event? Flipping the switch, or the light turning on?
how: A new way: an event is like a light switch. When you flip the switch, the light turns on. The flip is the event, and the light is the step.

key: COMP.PROG.L04.02|When clicked → say hi. What starts the program? A click, or saying hi?
how: A simpler step: one event, one step. When clicked → say hi. The click starts it.

key: COMP.PROG.L04.02|A game is split into these parts: start the music, move the player. How many parts is that? 2, or 5?
how: The skill underneath: Break It Down (Computing Level 4). A game is broken into small parts, and each event runs one small part.

key: COMP.PROG.L04.03|Which parts does every maze game need? A player, walls and a goal; just a title; or only music?
how: Now you put it all together and design your own maze game! A maze game has a player, walls and a goal. Arrow-key events move the player one square at a time. You plan it, code it, test it and fix it, just like real game makers!

how: Each arrow key gets its own event. When right arrow pressed → move right 1. You do the same for left, up and down.

COMP.PROG.L04.03|In the board game idea, what are the arrow keys? Your moves, or the walls?
how: A new way: a maze game is like a board game. The player is your game piece, the walls are lines you cannot cross, and the arrow keys are your moves.

key: COMP.PROG.L04.03|Look at the maze. Which key do you press to reach the flag? The right arrow, or the up arrow?
how: A simpler step: a tiny maze with no turns. The flag is straight across from the smiley.

key: COMP.PROG.L04.03|When left arrow pressed → move left 1. What is the event? Pressing the left arrow, or moving left?
how: The skill underneath: Events (Computing Level 4). Each arrow key press is an event, and the step under it moves the player.

key: COMP.DIG.L04.01|What is a document? A page you write on the computer, a game, or a mouse?
how: A document is a page you write on the computer, like a letter, a story or a report. You type, fix mistakes, and make it look great with a title and bold words. Your work is saved, so you can come back to it tomorrow. Let's become document pros!

key: COMP.DIG.L04.01|What does the blinking line, the cursor, show? Where the next letter goes, how loud the sound is, or the time?
how: The cursor is the blinking line. It shows where the next letter will go. Click where you want to type, and the cursor jumps there.
pic: Shabbos is coming|

key: COMP.DIG.L04.01|Look at the screen. The word comming has an extra m. Which key erases a letter before the cursor? Backspace, Enter, or Shift?
how: Backspace erases the letter just before the cursor. Made a mistake? Tap Backspace, then type the right letter.
pic: Shabbos is comming|

key: COMP.DIG.L04.01|In the notebook idea, what is Backspace? The eraser, or the pencil?
how: A new way: a document is like a notebook page that never runs out of erasers. Backspace is your eraser, and the cursor is the tip of your pencil.

key: COMP.DIG.L04.01|Look at the screen. You press Backspace one time. What is left? ca, or at?
how: A simpler step: just one key. Backspace erases one letter, the one right before the cursor.
pic: cat|

key: COMP.DIG.L04.01|Which sentence is ready for your document? "We love Shabbos.", or "we love shabbos"?
how: The skill underneath: Typing Sentences (Computing Level 4). A good document is built from good sentences: a capital to start, one space between words, and a period at the end.

key: COMP.DIG.L04.03|What are the small pieces of a message called? Packets, folders, or keys?
how: A big message is cut into small pieces called packets. Small pieces travel easily, and each one carries the address it is going to.

key: COMP.DIG.L04.03|In the puzzle idea, what are the puzzle pieces? The packets, or the routers?
how: A new way: sending a message is like mailing a big puzzle. You take it apart, put the address on every piece, mail the pieces, and your friend puts the puzzle back together.

key: COMP.DIG.L04.03|What helps a packet find the right computer? Its address, or its color?
how: A simpler step: just the address. Every packet carries an address, like a letter in the mail.

key: COMP.DIG.L04.03|Which one is hardware? A router, or a message?
how: The skill underneath: Hardware and Software (Computing Level 3). The cables, routers and computers are hardware. The message itself is made by software.

key: COMP.TYPE.L05.01|Look at the typing check. How many words did he type in one minute? 10, 44, or 40?
how: Good typists are fast AND careful. Speed is how many words you type in one minute. Accuracy is how many of your words are right. A careful typist who is a little slower beats a fast typist who makes many mistakes, because every mistake must be fixed. This year your goal is 15 words a minute with almost no mistakes.
pic: Typing check\nWords typed: 40\nMinutes: 4

key: COMP.TYPE.L05.01|Look at this typing check. How many words were typed right? 20, 22, or 18?
how: To count the right words, start with all the words typed and take away the words with a mistake.
pic: Typing check\nWords typed: 20\nWords with a mistake: 2

key: COMP.TYPE.L05.01|In the worked example, what do you divide by? The number of keys, the number of minutes, or the number of mistakes?
how: Worked example: Yossi typed 30 words in 2 minutes. 30 ÷ 2 = 15, so his speed is 15 words a minute. That is this year's goal!

COMP.TYPE.L05.01|In the balance beam idea, what is like falling off? Typing a capital letter, resting your hands, or making a mistake?
how: A new way: typing is like walking on a balance beam. If you run, you fall off and must start again. Walk carefully and you get there sooner.

key: COMP.TYPE.L05.01|How many words a minute is 20 words in 2 minutes? 22 or 10?
how: A simpler step: share the words between the minutes. 20 words in 2 minutes is 10 in each minute.

key: COMP.TYPE.L05.01|What did you type in Typing Sentences? Only the numbers on the top row; whole sentences with capitals and periods; or only single letters, one at a time?
how: The skill underneath: Typing Sentences (Computing Level 4). There you typed whole sentences with capitals and periods. Now you time them and count the mistakes.

key: COMP.PROG.L05.01|Look at the weather program. What does it say? Rain, Wear a cap, or Take a coat?
how: Programs make choices. An if block asks a yes-or-no question. If the answer is yes, the program does the blocks inside. If the answer is no, it does the else blocks instead. Games, apps and even the shul clock use if blocks to decide what to do.
pic:
when green flag clicked
set weather to "rain"
if weather = "rain" then
    say "Take a coat"
else
    say "Wear a cap"

key: COMP.PROG.L05.01|Look at the minyan program. What does it say? Start davening, 8, or Wait for more?
how: The if question can compare numbers. >= means "is at least". > means "is more than".
pic:
when green flag clicked
set men to 8
if men >= 10 then
    say "Start davening"
else
    say "Wait for more"

key: COMP.PROG.L05.01|Look at the Friday program. What does it say? Shut down before Shabbos, Friday, or Keep learning Gemara?
how: Worked example: day is "Friday". The if asks: is day "Friday"? Yes! So the program says the first message. If day were "Monday", the answer would be no, and it would say the else message.
pic:
when green flag clicked
set day to "Friday"
if day = "Friday" then
    say "Shut down before Shabbos"
else
    say "Keep learning Gemara"

key: COMP.PROG.L05.01|Look at the laps program. What does it say? Keep going, 5, or Great run?
pic:
when green flag clicked
set laps to 5
if laps > 3 then
    say "Great run"
else
    say "Keep going"

key: COMP.PROG.L05.01|Look at the number program. What does it say? Small, 7, or big?
pic:

set num to 7
if num > 10 then
    say "big"
else
    say "small"

pic:

    say "share"
if apples > 5 then
    say "plenty"

key: COMP.PROG.L05.01|What does an if block need? A picture of the screen, a yes-or-no question, or a number of minutes?
COMP.PROG.L05.01|Put the steps the computer takes for an if block in order. The cards say: Decide: yes or no. Run the matching part. Check the question.
COMP.PROG.L05.01|Zeidy's new program should light the porch lamp only when it is dark outside. Which block fits? Repeat 5 times turn the lamp on, if dark then turn the lamp on, or say lamp?
COMP.PROG.L05.01|Look at the traffic light program. What does it say? Go, Stop, or red?
pic:
when green flag clicked
set light to "red"
if light = "red" then
    say "Stop"
else
    say "Go"

key: COMP.PROG.L05.01|In an if-else, when does the else part run? Always, every time; when the answer is yes; or when the answer is no?
COMP.PROG.L05.01|If men were 12 in the minyan program, what would it say? 12, Start davening, or Wait for more?
pic:
when green flag clicked
set men to 8
if men >= 10 then
    say "Start davening"
else
    say "Wait for more"

key: COMP.PROG.L05.01|If it is sunny, what do you take? An umbrella or a cap?
how: A new way: an if block is like the rule "If it is raining, take an umbrella; else take a cap." You check the sky once and do one of the two.

key: COMP.PROG.L05.01|Is 5 more than 3? No or yes?
how: A simpler step: just answer the question. Is 5 more than 3?

key: COMP.PROG.L05.01|In Level 4, what does "when green flag clicked" do? Deletes the program, starts the program, or ends the program?
how: The skill underneath: Events (Computing Level 4). An event like "when green flag clicked" starts the program. Then the if blocks decide what happens next.

key: COMP.PROG.L05.02|Look at the score program. What does it say? 10, 0, or 5?
how: A variable is a box with a name that holds a number. Games use a variable called score. "set score to 0" puts 0 in the box. "change score by 5" adds 5 to what is already there. Variables let a program remember things, like how many questions you got right.
pic:
when green flag clicked
set score to 0
change score by 5
change score by 5
say score

key: COMP.PROG.L05.02|Look at the repeat program. What does it say? 5, 6, or 2?
how: A repeat block runs the blocks inside it again and again. "repeat 3 times" with "change score by 2" adds 2 three times.
pic:
when green flag clicked
set score to 0
repeat 3 times
    change score by 2
say score

key: COMP.PROG.L05.02|In the worked example, why did score change? The answer was right, score was already 1, or the program repeated?
how: Worked example: score starts at 0. answer is "Shabbos". The if asks: is answer "Shabbos"? Yes, so score changes by 1. Then say score shows 1. This is how a quiz game counts right answers!
pic:
when green flag clicked
set score to 0
set answer to "Shabbos"
if answer = "Shabbos" then
    change score by 1
say score

pic:

pic:

key: COMP.PROG.L05.02|Put the blocks of a simple score game in order. The cards say: change score by 1 say score set score to 0
COMP.PROG.L05.02|Shmuel makes a Chumash quiz game. Each right answer should add 1 to score. Which block goes inside the "right answer" if? Set score to 0, say "wrong", or change score by 1?
COMP.PROG.L05.02|Look at the stars program. What does it say? 2, 3, or 21?
pic:
when green flag clicked
set stars to 2
change stars by 1
say stars

key: COMP.PROG.L05.02|What is the difference between "set score to 5" and "change score by 5"? Set adds 5; change puts in 5, they always do the same thing, or set puts in 5; change adds 5?
COMP.PROG.L05.02|Why should a game start with "set score to 0"? So the score is always 0, so the game runs faster, or so every new game starts fresh?
COMP.PROG.L05.02|If the board shows 5 and you change it by 1, what does it show? 4 or 6?
how: A new way: a variable is like a counter on a shul's Omer board: you set it at the start, then move it up by one each night.

key: COMP.PROG.L05.02|Score is 3. After "change score by 2", what is score? 2 or 5?
how: A simpler step: just add one change. Score is 3. Change score by 2.

key: COMP.PROG.L05.02|In a quiz game, what does the if block check? If the answer is right, if the game is fun, or if the screen is on?
how: The skill underneath: If This, Then That (Computing Level 5). A quiz game uses an if block to check the answer, then changes the score.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.01|What should each slide have? Every idea at once, one main idea, or no words at all?
how: Slides help you teach other people: in class, at a Shabbos table or at a school assembly. A good slide has one idea, a short title, a few big words and a picture that helps. The people watching should listen to you, not read a long page. This skill makes your slides clear and easy to learn from.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.01|Which slide is easiest to read from the back of the room? Many tiny words, a full page of text, or a few big words?
how: Big words are easy to read from the back of the room. A few words are better than long sentences.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.01|Which picture fits a slide about the Bais Medrash schedule? A funny cartoon that has no link to it; a simple chart of the times; or no picture, just a full page of text?
COMP.DIG.L05.01|Which is the best title for a slide about saving the computer's work? Save Your Work, Slide, or Some Things About Computers and Other Stuff?
COMP.DIG.L05.01|While you present, what should you do? Read every word on the slide out loud, talk to the listeners and explain, or face the screen with your back to them?
COMP.DIG.L05.01|Your slide has six sentences in small letters. How do you fix it? Keep a few key words and make them big, add three more sentences, or make the letters even smaller?
COMP.DIG.L05.01|Put Eli's matzah slides in order. The cards say: Mix flour and water Roll and bake fast Summary Title: How Matzah Is Baked
COMP.DIG.L05.01|How many main ideas go on one slide? One, five, or ten?
COMP.DIG.L05.01|Which slide is the clearest? A long paragraph in tiny letters and no title at all; a short title, a few big words and a helpful picture; or only a big title and nothing else under it?
COMP.DIG.L05.01|What goes on the last slide of a teaching show? A blank page, a brand-new topic, or a short summary?
COMP.DIG.L05.01|In the sign idea, what makes a good slide? Long and full of detail or short and clear?
how: A new way: a slide is like a sign at a simcha hall. It says only what you need, big and clear: "Kiddush this way". Nobody stops to read a long story on a sign.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.01|Which is a better slide title? Washing Hands or This Slide Is All About the Way We Wash Our Hands?
how: A simpler step: just choose the shorter title. A good title is a few words.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.01|What did you write in Write a Document? Full sentences and paragraphs, only pictures with no words, or only one word on each page?
how: The skill underneath: Write a Document (Computing Level 4). In a document you write full paragraphs. On a slide you keep only the key words.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.02|What does giving credit mean? Paying for every picture, hiding where you found it, or writing who made the work?
how: Every picture, song, story and program was made by someone. Using another person's work and saying it is yours is not honest. Before you use something, ask if you are allowed, and always write who made it. This is called giving credit. It shows respect for the person who worked hard on it.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.02|Which is a good credit line? My own picture I found, Picture by Moshe Klein, or Picture from somewhere?
how: A credit line says who made something, like "Picture by Moshe Klein" or "Story from the school library book Bais Hamikdash".

key: COMP.DIG.L05.02|In the worked example, what did Avi do first? He asked Tzvi if he may use it, he said he drew it, or he copied it without asking?
how: Worked example: Avi wants a drawing of a sukkah for his report. His friend Tzvi drew one. Avi asks Tzvi, "May I use it?" Tzvi says yes. Avi puts it in and writes "Drawing by Tzvi". He asked AND gave credit.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.02|Dov copies a paragraph from a book into his report and does not say where it came from. Is that OK? Yes, if nobody finds out; yes, books are free to copy; or no, he must say where it came from?

COMP.DIG.L05.02|You find a picture inside the class app's picture library marked "free for school use". What should you do? Use it and hide the name, use it and write where it came from, or say you drew it yourself?
COMP.DIG.L05.02|Which shows respect for another boy's work? Asking first and giving credit, changing one color and calling it yours, or using it without asking?
COMP.DIG.L05.02|Your rebbe says you may use his chart in your slides. What else should you do? Write "Chart by Rabbi Weiss", remove his name from it, or nothing else at all?
COMP.DIG.L05.02|Put the steps for using someone else's picture in order. The cards say: Ask if you may use it. Write a credit line. Find out who made it.

COMP.DIG.L05.02|Yehuda made a great program and Baruch shows it to the class saying "I made this". What is wrong? Nothing is wrong with that, Baruch took credit for Yehuda's work, or Yehuda should not have made it?
COMP.DIG.L05.02|What should you write under a picture you did not make? Who made it, nothing, or your own name?
COMP.DIG.L05.02|Why do we give credit? It makes the report longer, the computer needs it to work, or it is honest and respects the maker?
COMP.DIG.L05.02|Before using another boy's drawing, what do you do? Ask him if you may, wait until he leaves, or just take it?
COMP.DIG.L05.02|In the lunch idea, what is the right thing to do? Take it quietly and say nothing about it or ask first and say whose it is?
how: A new way: using someone's work without credit is like eating someone else's lunch and saying it was yours. Even if it tastes good, it is not yours.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.02|In "Drawing by Tzvi", who made the drawing? The drawing or Tzvi?
how: A simpler step: just name the maker. "Song by Chaim" names Chaim.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.02|What did Ask Before You Click teach? To never use a computer, to click everything fast, or to ask before you click or use something?
how: The skill underneath: Ask Before You Click (Computing Level 3). There you learned to ask a grown-up before clicking. Here you ask before using someone's work.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.03|Look at the password. What is wrong with it? It is too short, it has no letters, or nothing; it is strong?
how: A password is the key to your account. A strong password is long, mixes in numbers and symbols, and is not your name or birthday. A great trick is to join a few random words, like blue-kugel-77!. Keep it secret: share it only with Abba or your teacher, and never type it into a message or a pop-up.
pic: Rule: at least 12 characters\nPassword: kugel

key: COMP.DIG.L05.03|Look at blue-kugel-train. What is it missing? It is too short, it has no number, or it has no letters?
how: A long password made of words is good, but the rules also ask for a number and a symbol, like 7 or !.
pic: Rules: at least 12 characters, a number, a symbol\nPassword: blue-kugel-train

key: COMP.DIG.L05.03|Look at the worked example's password. What is missing? Nothing; it is strong, it has no symbol, or it has no number?
how: Worked example: blue-kugel-77! has 14 characters, a number (7) and symbols (- and !). It is not a name or a birthday. It passes every rule, and it is easy to remember because it is a silly picture: a blue kugel.
pic: Rules: at least 12 characters, a number, a symbol\nPassword: blue-kugel-77!

key: COMP.DIG.L05.03|Look at greentrainshul. What is it missing? Nothing; it is strong, it has no number, or it is too short?
pic: Rules: at least 12 characters, a number, a symbol\nPassword: greentrainshul

key: COMP.DIG.L05.03|Which password is strongest? ChaimKlein2016, password12345, or purple-sukkah-42!?
COMP.DIG.L05.03|Who may you share your password with? Abba or your teacher, anyone who asks in a message, or your best friend?
COMP.DIG.L05.03|A pop-up says "Type your password to win a prize". What do you do? Type your password quickly, send it to a friend, or close it and tell Abba or your teacher?
COMP.DIG.L05.03|Put the steps for making a strong password in order. The cards say: Join them with symbols. Add a number. Pick a few random words.

COMP.DIG.L05.03|Moshe wants to use his name and birthday as his password because it is easy to remember. What should he do instead? Use the word password, use his name with no birthday, or join random words with a number and a symbol?
COMP.DIG.L05.03|Why is "Chaim2016" a weak password? It has far too many symbols in it, it uses a name and a year others can guess, or it is much too long to type every day?
COMP.DIG.L05.03|What is the best way to keep a password safe? Write it on the screen of the computer, keep it secret and never type it into a pop-up, or tell it to the whole class?
COMP.DIG.L05.03|How many characters should a strong password have, at least? 3, 5, or 12?
COMP.DIG.L05.03|In the key idea, who should get a copy? Only the people who keep you safe or anyone at all who asks you for it?
how: A new way: a password is like the key to your family's front door. You do not hand copies to strangers, and a key that is easy to copy is not safe.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.03|Is 5 at least 12? Yes or no?
how: A simpler step: just count. "kugel" has 5 letters. Is 5 at least 12?

key: COMP.DIG.L05.03|What did My Password Is Mine teach? Your password is private, passwords are not needed, or everyone shares one password?
how: The skill underneath: My Password Is Mine (Computing Level 2). There you learned a password is private. Now you learn to make it strong.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.04|Look at the bits under the places 4, 2 and 1. What number do they make? 5, 3, or 101?
how: Inside every computer, everything is stored as 0s and 1s, called bits. A bit is like a light that is off (0) or on (1). With a few bits a computer can write any number, and with numbers it can store letters, pictures and sounds. Learning to read bits lets you see how a computer really thinks.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.04|Look at 1 1 0. What number is it? 110, 6, or 3?
how: Each place is double the one to its right: 1, 2, 4, 8. A 1 means "count this place"; a 0 means "skip it".

key: COMP.DIG.L05.04|Look at the worked example. Which places are on? All four, 4 and 2, or 8 and 1?
how: Worked example: 1 0 0 1 under 8, 4, 2, 1. The 8 is on, the 4 and 2 are off, the 1 is on. 8 + 1 = 9.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.04|Look at 1 1 1 1. What number is it? 15, 1111, or 4?
COMP.DIG.L05.04|Look at 0 1 1. What number is it? 6, 3, or 11?
COMP.DIG.L05.04|Look at 1 0 1 0. What number is it? 10, 5, or 1010?
COMP.DIG.L05.04|What are the only two digits a computer uses inside? 0 and 1, 1 and 2, or 0 to 9?
COMP.DIG.L05.04|Put the place values for 4 bits in order, from left to right. The cards say: 4 2 1 8
COMP.DIG.L05.04|Ari's calculator stores the number of boys in his class, 9, inside the computer. How is 9 written in 4 bits? 1111, 0110, or 1001?
COMP.DIG.L05.04|Look at 1 0 under 2 and 1. What number is it? 2, 10, or 1?
COMP.DIG.L05.04|Look at 1 0 1 again. What number is it? 6, 2, or 5?
COMP.DIG.L05.04|What is a bit? A key on the keyboard, one 0 or 1 inside the computer, or a small screen picture?
COMP.DIG.L05.04|Lamps worth 4 and 1 are on. What number is that? 5 or 41?
how: A new way: think of 4 lamps in a row worth 8, 4, 2 and 1. Turn some on and add the lamps that are lit.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.04|A 1 sits under the 4 place. What does it count as? 1 or 4?
how: A simpler step: one bit at a time. A 1 under the 2 place counts as 2.

key: COMP.DIG.L05.04|In How Messages Travel, what were messages split into? Whole books, small packets, or paper letters?
how: The skill underneath: How Messages Travel (Computing Level 4). Messages travel as tiny packets, and every packet is made of 0s and 1s.

key: COMP.TYPE.L06.01|Which two keys have small bumps to help you find home row? F and J, A and L, or G and H?
how: Your fingers start on the home row. Find the small bumps on two keys with your pointer fingers, and you can find home without looking.
pic: A S D F   J K L ;

key: COMP.TYPE.L06.01|Avi typed 120 words in 4 minutes. How many words per minute is that? 30, 480, or 116?
how: Speed is measured in words per minute. Divide the number of words by the number of minutes. 60 words in 2 minutes is 30 words per minute.

key: COMP.TYPE.L06.01|Which matters more while you are learning to type? Accuracy first, speed first, or looking at your fingers?
COMP.TYPE.L06.01|Shmuli typed 90 words in 3 minutes. How many words per minute? 30, 27, or 93?
COMP.TYPE.L06.01|Mendy typed 50 words and made 5 mistakes. How many words were typed correctly? 45, 55, or 10?
COMP.TYPE.L06.01|Put the steps in order to practice a typing drill. The cards say: Check your speed and mistakes., Put your fingers on home row., Type the drill with eyes on the screen.

COMP.TYPE.L06.01|Yehuda types his dvar Torah for the Shabbos table. He keeps looking down at the keys and loses his place. What should he practice? Keeping his eyes on the screen, typing with one finger very slowly, or typing with the lights turned off?
COMP.TYPE.L06.01|Eli typed 160 words in 4 minutes. How many words per minute? 40, 164, or 156?
COMP.TYPE.L06.01|Which key does your right little finger rest on? The semicolon key, the J key, or the space bar?
pic: J K L ;

key: COMP.TYPE.L06.01|Why do fast typists keep their eyes on the screen? To catch mistakes as they type, because the keys are too bright, or to type slower?
COMP.TYPE.L06.01|In the stairs idea, what are your feet like? Your fingers, or your eyes?
how: A new way: touch typing is like walking up the stairs at home in the dark. Your feet know where each step is, so you do not need to look.

key: COMP.TYPE.L06.01|20 words in 2 minutes. How many words per minute? 10, or 22?
how: A simpler step: just divide. Words per minute is the words shared equally among the minutes.

key: COMP.TYPE.L06.01|Which sentence is typed correctly? "Chaim learns Gemara.", or "chaim learns gemara"?
how: The skill underneath: Typing Sentences (Computing Level 4). Fluent typing is still built from good sentences: a capital, one space between words, and a period.

key: COMP.PROG.L06.01|Why make your own block? To reuse a group of steps by one name, to make the program longer and bigger, or to hide the green flag from players?
how: Sometimes you use the same group of steps again and again. Programmers wrap those steps in a new block with its own name, like draw square. Then one block does the whole job, anywhere in your program. Fewer blocks, fewer mistakes, and the program is easier to read!

key: COMP.PROG.L06.01|Look at the block. What does draw square do each time it runs? Moves and turns 4 times, moves 50 and then stops at once, or turns around and plays a sound?
how: Look at this block. Its name is draw square. Inside it are the steps: repeat 4 times, move 50 and turn 90.
pic:
define draw square
  repeat 4
    move 50
    turn 90

key: COMP.PROG.L06.01|The block is jump (n). Which one makes the player jump 5 times? jump (5), jump (n), or jump (3)?
how: An input is a blank in your block that you fill in each time, like jump (n). jump (3) jumps 3 times, and jump (5) jumps 5 times.

key: COMP.PROG.L06.01|Look at the program. It uses draw square 3 times. How many times does move 50 run in all? 12, 3, or 15?
pic:
define draw square
  repeat 4
    move 50
    turn 90

When green flag clicked
  draw square
  draw square
  draw square

key: COMP.PROG.L06.01|Which is the best name for a block that draws a star? draw star, block 1, or my stuff?

COMP.PROG.L06.01|Dovid copies the same 6 blocks into his game 5 times. What is a better way? Make one new block and use it 5 times, copy all 6 blocks in 10 more times, or start the whole game over again?
COMP.PROG.L06.01|The block greet (name) says Shalom and then the name. Which call makes it say Shalom Yossi? greet (Yossi), greet (name), or say (Yossi)?
COMP.PROG.L06.01|Put the steps in order to make your own block. The cards say: Use the block in your program., Name the new block., Put the steps inside it.

COMP.PROG.L06.01|Every Erev Shabbos, Shmuli does the same jobs: set the table, put out the candlesticks, fold the napkins. Abba calls it the Shabbos setup. How is that name like a new block? One name stands for many steps, it makes the jobs take longer, or it lets him skip the jobs?
COMP.PROG.L06.01|Look at the program. How many times does turn 90 run? 8, 2, or 4?
pic:
define draw square
  repeat 4
    move 50
    turn 90

When green flag clicked
  draw square
  draw square

key: COMP.PROG.L06.01|What is an input in a block? A blank you fill in each time, the name written on the block, or the green flag that starts it?

COMP.PROG.L06.01|Chaim's block draw house has a bug. He fixes it inside the block. Where is it fixed? Everywhere draw house is used, only in the first place it is used, or nowhere until he fixes each one?
COMP.PROG.L06.01|In the recipe idea, what is the block name? The title on the card, or one step on the card?
how: A new way: your own block is like a recipe card. The card is called kugel, and all the steps are on it. You just say make kugel instead of reading every step aloud.

key: COMP.PROG.L06.01|A block has 2 steps inside. You use it 2 times. How many steps run? 4, or 2?
how: A simpler step: one block, used two times. Inside it are 2 steps.

key: COMP.PROG.L06.01|Which is a good small part to make into its own block in a maze game? Move the player one square, or the whole game?
how: The skill underneath: Break It Down (Computing Level 4). A new block is one small part of a big job, given its own name.

key: COMP.PROG.L06.02|What is a list in a program? Many items kept in order under one name, one number that can never change, or a picture drawn on the screen?
how: A variable holds one thing. A list holds many things under one name, in order, like a shopping list. Games use lists for questions, players and high scores. You can add items, find an item by its number, and count how many are in the list. Let's learn lists!

key: COMP.PROG.L06.02|Look at the list. What is item 3 of shopping? Fish, challah, or candles?
how: Each item has a number that tells its place. Item 1 is first. To find item 3, count down to the third line.
pic:
list: shopping
1  challah
2  grape juice
3  fish
4  candles

key: COMP.PROG.L06.02|Look at the list. You add apples to shopping. What is the length now? 5, 4, or 6?
how: The length of a list is how many items it has. Add an item, and the length grows by one.
pic:
list: shopping
1  challah
2  grape juice
3  fish
4  candles

3  Demai

key: COMP.PROG.L06.02|Look at the list. What is the length of names? 5, 4, or 6?
pic:

5  Chaim

key: COMP.PROG.L06.02|Look at the list. Which item number is Eli? 4, 3, or 5?
pic:

4  Eli
5  Chaim

pic:
list: mishnayos
1  Brachos
2  Peah
3  Demai

key: COMP.PROG.L06.02|Put the steps in order to add a new player to a game list. The cards say: Show the new length., Ask for the player's name., Add the name to the list.

COMP.PROG.L06.02|Abba keeps a list of guests for the Shabbos seudah. Three guests are on it, and then the Cohens call to say they are coming. What happens to the list? One item is added and the length is 4, nothing changes and it stays at 3 guests, or the whole list is erased and restarted?
COMP.PROG.L06.02|Look at the list. What is item 4 of names? Eli, Yossi, or Chaim?
pic:
list: names
1  Moshe
2  Dovid
3  Yossi
4  Eli
5  Chaim

key: COMP.PROG.L06.02|Why use a list instead of 20 separate variables? One name holds them all in order, lists are slower, or variables cannot hold names?
COMP.PROG.L06.02|Look at the list. You add matches to shopping. What is item 5 now? Matches, candles, or fish?
pic:
list: shopping
1  challah
2  grape juice
3  fish
4  candles

key: COMP.PROG.L06.02|In the cubby idea, what is the cubby number? The item's place in the list, or the item itself?
how: A new way: a list is like a row of numbered cubbies in your classroom. Each cubby has a number and holds one thing.

key: COMP.PROG.L06.02|Look at the list. What is item 2? Lulav, or esrog?
how: A simpler step: a short list of two. Item 1 is first, and item 2 is second.
pic: list: sukkos\n1  esrog\n2  lulav

key: COMP.PROG.L06.02|Which belongs in a list called fruits? Apple, or hammer?
how: The skill underneath: Sort It Out (Computing Level 3). A list keeps sorted things together, so you can count them and find them.

key: COMP.PROG.L06.03|What should you do before you start coding a big program? Make a plan, start dragging blocks, or skip testing?
how: Real programmers plan before they code. They say the goal, write the steps in plain words, and sometimes draw a flowchart. Plain-word steps are called pseudocode. A good plan saves hours of fixing, because you find problems on paper first. Let's plan like pros!

key: COMP.PROG.L06.03|Which line is pseudocode? If the answer is right, add 1 to the score; move 10 steps, then turn 15 degrees; or 01001 10110 00111?
how: Pseudocode means writing the steps in plain words, not in code. It is a plan anyone can read.

key: COMP.PROG.L06.03|Look at the shapes. Which shape asks a yes-or-no question? The diamond, the oval, or the rectangle?
how: A flowchart shows steps as shapes. An oval starts or ends it, a rectangle is a step, and a diamond asks a yes-or-no question. Arrows show which way to go.
pic:
Flowchart shapes:
⬭ = start or end
▭ = a step
◇ = a question

COMP.PROG.L06.03|Before Pesach, Zeidy writes a plan: what to clean, who cleans it, and in what order. How is that like planning a program? Writing the steps first saves mistakes later, it wastes time that could be spent cleaning, or it only works for computers and not people?

key: COMP.PROG.L06.03|Put the top of the flowchart in order. The cards say: Is the answer right?, Start, Ask the question.
COMP.PROG.L06.03|In the map idea, what is the place you are driving to? The goal of the program, or the bugs?
how: A new way: a plan is like a map before a trip. You decide where you are going and which roads to take before you start driving.

key: COMP.PROG.L06.03|Which is a goal sentence? My game lets a player catch falling apples, or blocks blocks blocks?
how: A simpler step: just the goal. A goal says in one sentence what the program should do.

key: COMP.PROG.L06.03|Which is a small step of the goal make a quiz game? Write the first question, or finish everything at once?
how: The skill underneath: Break It Down (Computing Level 4). A plan breaks the big goal into small steps you can code one at a time.

how: A new way: a spreadsheet is like a seating chart. Each seat has a row and a column, and you find a seat by its name, like B3.

key: COMP.DIG.L06.02|Why must you judge a website before trusting it? Anyone can post anything online, every website is checked and true, or websites can never change?
how: Anyone can put anything on the internet, true or not. A smart researcher judges every source before trusting it. Ask four questions: Who wrote it? When was it written? Why was it written? Can I find the same fact in another good source? Then you will know what to trust!

key: COMP.DIG.L06.02|Which source is most likely to be right about whales? A science museum page, an ad for toys, or a page with no author?
how: Check who wrote it. A museum, a university or an expert usually knows the topic. A page with no author is harder to trust.

key: COMP.DIG.L06.02|Look at the two pages. You want the newest facts about Chromebooks. Which page is better? The 2026 page, or the 2012 page?
how: Check when it was written. For news, or for science that keeps changing, a newer date is usually better.
pic: Page A: Chromebook guide — updated 2026\nPage B: Chromebook guide — written 2012

how: A new way: judging a source is like checking the hechsher on food. You look at who stands behind it before you trust it.

key: COMP.DIG.L06.02|Which page is easier to trust? A page by a doctor about health, or a page with no name?
how: A simpler step: just the author. A page from an expert is easier to trust than a page from no one.

key: COMP.DIG.L06.02|A message travels to you through many routers. Can you see who wrote it just by reading it? Not always, or always?
how: The skill underneath: How Messages Travel (Computing Level 4). Messages reach you from computers all over the world, so you cannot see who sent them unless you check.

key: COMP.PROG.L06.04|What does the score variable count in a quiz game? Right answers, wrong keys, or the screen color?
how: Now you build a real quiz game! It keeps its questions in a list, asks each one, and checks the answer. A variable called score counts the right answers. Every right answer changes score by 1. You will plan it, build it, test it, and share it with your friends!

key: COMP.PROG.L06.04|Look at the program. What does the first if block check? Whether answer equals 7, whether the flag is green, or how fast he types?
how: The ask block shows a question and waits. Whatever the player types is saved in answer. An if block checks it.
pic:
When green flag clicked
  set score to 0
  ask "How many days are in a week?" and wait
  if answer = 7 then change score by 1
  ask "What is the first letter of the aleph-beis?" and wait
  if answer = Aleph then change score by 1

key: COMP.PROG.L06.04|Why does the game set score to 0 at the start? So each game starts fresh, to make the game a lot harder, or to end the game right away?
how: At the start of the game, set score to 0. Otherwise the score from the last game would still be there.

how: A new way: a quiz game is like your rebbe giving a chazara quiz. He asks, waits for your answer, checks it, and marks it.

key: COMP.TYPE.L07.01|Yossi types the same Shabbos menu every week for Abba. What saves him the most time? Copy last week's menu and paste it, retype the whole menu every week, or print a blank page and write it?

COMP.TYPE.L07.01|Why do fast workers use shortcuts? They save time compared to menus, they make the screen bigger, or they type in color?
COMP.TYPE.L07.01|In the path idea, what is walking around the field? Clicking through menus, or pressing Ctrl + C?
how: A new way: a shortcut is like a path across a field instead of walking all the way around it. You get to the same place, faster.

key: COMP.TYPE.L07.01|Which two keys have bumps so you can find home row without looking? F and J, or Q and P?
how: The skill underneath: Touch Typing Fluency (Computing Level 6). Shortcuts are fastest when your fingers already know where the keys are.

key: COMP.PROG.L07.01|What is text code? Blocks written as typed words, a picture of the blocks on screen, or a secret message for friends?
how: Blocks are great for learning, but real programmers type their code as words. Each block becomes a line of text, like move(10) or print("Shalom"). Text code is faster to write and can do much more. You already know the ideas; now you learn to write them!

key: COMP.PROG.L07.01|Look at the program. What does it show first? Shalom, Good morning, or print?
how: print shows words on the screen. The words go inside quote marks, inside the parentheses. Lines run from top to bottom.
pic: print(\"Shalom\")\nprint(\"Good morning\")

key: COMP.PROG.L07.01|Look at the program. What does it print? 7, 4, or x?
how: A variable holds a value. x = 4 puts 4 in x. x = x + 3 takes what is in x and adds 3.
pic: x = 4\nx = x + 3\nprint(x)

COMP.PROG.L07.01|In the letter idea, what are the blocks like? Pointing at pictures, or writing words?
how: A new way: text code is like writing a letter instead of pointing at pictures. The meaning is the same; you just use words.

key: COMP.PROG.L07.01|What does print("Hi") show? Hi, or print?
how: A simpler step: one line. print("Hi") shows what is inside the quote marks.

key: COMP.PROG.L07.01|The block is jump (n). Which text jumps 3 times? jump(3), or jump(n)?
how: The skill underneath: Build Your Own Block (Computing Level 6). A block with an input, like jump (n), becomes text like jump(3).

key: COMP.PROG.L07.02|In text code, when do the indented lines under if run? When the test is true, every time the program runs, or only when the test is false?
how: Programs make choices and repeat things. In text code, if checks a test, and the indented lines under it run only when the test is true. else catches everything else. for and while repeat lines. These few words power almost every game and app!

key: COMP.PROG.L07.02|Look at the program. What does it print? Great, Try again, or both?
how: Check the test with the real number. If it passes, run the lines under if. If not, run the lines under else.

key: COMP.DIG.L07.01|What happens to a formula when you change one of its numbers? It updates by itself, it breaks, or it stays the same?
how: You already know =SUM. Spreadsheets have many more formulas. =AVERAGE finds the middle value, =MAX finds the biggest, =MIN finds the smallest, and =COUNT tells how many numbers there are. Change a number and every formula updates by itself. That is why scientists and businesses love spreadsheets!

key: COMP.DIG.L07.02|Where does a computer keep your saved files for tomorrow? In storage, on the screen, or in the speaker?
COMP.DIG.L07.02|Which device does both input and output? A touchscreen, a speaker, or a printer?

COMP.DIG.L07.02|At the grocery checkout, the cashier scans the challah, the screen shows the price, and the receipt prints. Which part is output? The screen and the receipt, the scanner at the register, or the challah being scanned?
COMP.DIG.L07.02|Which one is storage? A hard drive, a mouse, or a speaker?
COMP.DIG.L07.02|What is the CPU? The processor that does the work, the screen that shows the picture, or the case around all the parts?
COMP.DIG.L07.02|In the kitchen idea, what is the fridge? Storage, or output?
how: A new way: a computer is like a kitchen. Groceries come in, the cook works on them, the meal goes out to the table, and leftovers go in the fridge.

key: COMP.DIG.L07.03|What is a digital footprint? The trail of what you do online, the size of a shoe you buy online, or a part inside a computer?
how: Every message, photo and comment you put online leaves a trail called a digital footprint. Others can copy it or take a screenshot, and it can last for years, even after you delete it. A good footprint shows kindness and good middos. Think before you post!

key: COMP.DIG.L07.03|Eli deletes an unkind message he sent. Is it surely gone forever? No, yes, or only on Tuesdays?
how: When you delete a post, copies may still exist: someone may have saved it or taken a screenshot.

key: COMP.DIG.L07.03|What is a good test before posting? Would my rebbe be proud of it, will it get a lot of likes, or is it funny to my friends?
how: Before you post, ask: would my parents and my rebbe be proud of this? If not, do not post it.

key: COMP.DIG.L07.03|Which post is safest for your footprint? A kind birthday wish to a friend, a mean joke about a classmate, or your home address?
COMP.DIG.L07.03|Why can a post last for years? People can copy or screenshot it, posts fade like ink, or computers forget everything?
COMP.DIG.L07.03|A classmate shares an embarrassing photo of another boy. What should you do? Do not share it and tell a grown-up, share it with just a few friends, or add a funny comment under it?
COMP.DIG.L07.03|Which fact should stay off your footprint? Your school's name and schedule, that you like baseball, or your favorite sefer?
COMP.DIG.L07.03|Put the steps in order before posting. The cards say: Post only if it passes., Stop and read it again., Ask: is it kind and safe?

COMP.DIG.L07.03|Shmuli's cousin wants to post a video of their family's Chanukah party. What should he do first? Ask everyone in it for permission, post it right away while it is fresh, or add funny music and then post it?
COMP.DIG.L07.03|What does think before you post mean? Check that it is kind and safe first, post faster than everyone else, or never use a computer again?
COMP.DIG.L07.03|Does deleting a post always remove every copy? No, yes, or only for photos?
COMP.DIG.L07.03|Which builds a good digital footprint? Helpful, kind comments; rude replies; or sharing secrets?
COMP.DIG.L07.03|In the cement idea, what is the dried footprint? A post that stays online, or a post you never made?
how: A new way: a digital footprint is like footprints in wet cement. Once they dry, they are very hard to remove.

key: COMP.DIG.L07.03|Which message is kind? Great job on your siyum, or that was a dumb answer?
how: A simpler step: one question. Is it kind?

key: COMP.DIG.L07.03|Which is private? Your password, or your favorite color?
how: The skill underneath: Strong Passwords (Computing Level 5). Keeping private facts private protects your footprint too.

key: COMP.TYPE.L08.01|Look at the keys. Which keys type an exclamation mark? Shift + 1, Shift + 4, or just 1?
how: Hold Shift and tap a number key to type the symbol printed above it.

key: COMP.TYPE.L08.01|Look at the keys. Which keys type the at sign? Shift + 2, Shift + 3, or Ctrl + A?
COMP.TYPE.L08.01|Look at the keys. Which keys type a dollar sign? Shift + 4, Shift + 1, or Shift + S?
COMP.TYPE.L08.01|Put the steps in order to type a number without looking. The cards say: Return to home row., Find home row with the bumps., Reach up and tap the number.
COMP.TYPE.L08.01|Yossi types the tzedakah total for his class: $25. Which keys make the dollar sign? Shift + 4, Shift + 2, or Shift + 5?
COMP.TYPE.L08.01|Look at the keys. Which keys type a hashtag sign? Shift + 3, Shift + 1, or Shift + 9?
COMP.TYPE.L08.01|Why reach up and come back to home row? So your fingers always know where they are, so you can type slower and calmer, or so your thumbs can rest on the keys?
COMP.TYPE.L08.01|In the shelf idea, where do your fingers stand? The home row, or the top shelf?
how: A new way: the number row is like the top shelf. Your fingers stand on the home row, reach up to the shelf, then step back down.

key: COMP.TYPE.L08.01|Look at the keys. Shift + 1 types which symbol? !, or 1?
how: A simpler step: one symbol. Shift with a number key types the symbol printed on top.

key: COMP.DIG.L08.01|Why format a document? To make it easier to read, to make it look longer, or to hide the mistakes?
how: A document can have great ideas and still be hard to read. Formatting fixes that: headings show the main parts, bullet lists break up long lines, and one steady font makes it look clean. Teachers, businesses and yeshivos all expect neat documents. Let's format like a pro!

key: COMP.DIG.L08.01|What is a heading? A short title for a section, the last sentence on the page, or the number at the bottom of a page?
how: A heading is a short title for a section. It is bigger or bolder than the body text, so readers can find each part.

key: COMP.DIG.L08.01|Which fits a numbered list best? Steps to bake challah, a list of favorite colors, or one long story?
how: Bullets list short items, each on its own line with a dot in front. Numbered lists are for steps that go in order.

key: COMP.DIG.L08.01|Moshe uses five different fonts on one page. What is the problem? It looks messy and is hard to read, it uses too little ink to print, or there is no problem with that?
COMP.DIG.L08.01|Which should be bigger than the body text? A heading, a page number, or a footnote?
COMP.DIG.L08.01|Dovid presses Enter five times to make space between paragraphs. What is a better way? Use paragraph spacing, press Enter ten times, or delete the paragraphs?
COMP.DIG.L08.01|Which items fit a bullet list? Things to pack for camp, a letter to Zeidy, or a long story about camp?
COMP.DIG.L08.01|Put the steps in order to format a report. The cards say: Add headings for each part., Type the text first., Check the whole page.

COMP.DIG.L08.01|Yehuda types the schedule for the Purim mesibah: times and activities. What format helps people read it fast? A list with times and bold headings, one long paragraph with everything, or all capital letters so it is loud?
COMP.DIG.L08.01|What does a numbered list show? Steps in order, the most important word, or a picture?
COMP.DIG.L08.01|Why use the same font for all the body text? It looks neat and steady, it is required by law, or it saves electricity?
COMP.DIG.L08.01|Which is the best heading for a report section about Chanukah? Chanukah Customs, some More Words, or section Number 3?
COMP.DIG.L08.01|In the table idea, what is like the food? The words, or the formatting?
how: A new way: formatting is like setting the Shabbos table neatly. The same food looks better when it is served nicely.

key: COMP.DIG.L08.01|How do you make a heading stand out? Bigger and bold, or tiny and gray?
how: A simpler step: one heading. Make it bigger and bold so it stands out.

key: COMP.DIG.L08.01|Where are the number keys? On the top row, or on the home row?
how: The skill underneath: Numbers and Symbols (Computing Level 8). Numbered lists and dates in documents need the number row.

key: COMP.PROG.L08.01|Look at the program. What does it say? 12, 6, or 36?
how: Look at the function double. It takes n and reports n times 2. Calling double(6) puts 6 in for n.
pic:
define double (n)
  report n * 2

say double(6)

key: COMP.PROG.L08.01|Look at the program. What does add(4, 5) say? 9, 45, or 1?
how: A function can take two inputs. add(4, 5) puts 4 in for a and 5 in for b.
pic:
define add (a, b)
  report a + b

say add(4, 5)

key: COMP.PROG.L08.01|Look at the program. What does double(double(3)) say? 12, 6, or 18?
pic:
define double (n)
  report n * 2

say double(double(3))

key: COMP.PROG.L08.01|Look at the program. What does area(5, 4) say? 20, 9, or 54?
pic:
define area (w, h)
  report w * h

say area(5, 4)

key: COMP.PROG.L08.01|Look at the program. What does double(add(2, 3)) say? 10, 7, or 23?
pic:
define add (a, b)
  report a + b
define double (n)
  report n * 2

say double(add(2, 3))

key: COMP.PROG.L08.01|What is the input in double(8)? 8, double, or 16?
COMP.PROG.L08.01|Put the steps in order when a function is called. The cards say: Report the answer., Put the inputs in for the names., Do the steps inside.

COMP.PROG.L08.01|At the bakery, you hand over money and say how many challos you want, and the baker hands back challos and change. How is that like a function? Inputs go in and an answer comes back, it repeats the same order forever, or nothing at all comes back to you?
COMP.PROG.L08.01|Look at the program. What does triple(7) say? 21, 10, or 73?
pic:
define triple (n)
  report n * 3

say triple(7)

key: COMP.PROG.L08.01|How is a function with report different from a plain block? It sends back an answer, it has no name, or it cannot have inputs?
COMP.PROG.L08.01|Why use functions in a big program? Write a job once and reuse it, make the program much longer, or slow the whole program down?
COMP.PROG.L08.01|In the juicer idea, what is the output? The juice, or the oranges?
how: A new way: a function is like a juicer. Oranges go in, and juice comes out. Different oranges, different juice, same machine.

key: COMP.PROG.L08.01|A function adds 1 to its input. The input is 9. What is reported? 10, or 9?
how: A simpler step: add one. If the function adds 1, an input of 4 gives back 5.

key: COMP.PROG.L08.01|The block jump (n) has an input. Which call jumps 4 times? jump (4), or jump (n)?
how: The skill underneath: Build Your Own Block (Computing Level 6). A function is your own block that also reports an answer.

key: COMP.PROG.L08.02|What is an algorithm? A step-by-step way to solve a problem, a type of keyboard used for coding, or a program that is broken and stuck?
how: An algorithm is a step-by-step way to solve a problem. Two famous jobs are searching, finding an item in a list, and sorting, putting a list in order. Computers search and sort millions of items a second. Smart algorithms finish with fewer steps. Let's think like computer scientists!

key: COMP.PROG.L08.02|Look at the list. How many items are checked to find 9? 3, 1, or 4?
how: Linear search checks item 1, then item 2, and so on, until it finds what it wants.
pic: list = [7, 3, 9, 4]\nsearch for 9, starting at item 1

key: COMP.PROG.L08.02|Look at the list. What is it after sorting? 4, 9, 12; 12, 9, 4; or 9, 4, 12?
how: Sorting puts items in order. Smallest to largest is called ascending.
pic: list = [12, 4, 9]\nsort smallest to largest

key: COMP.PROG.L08.02|Look at the list. How many items are checked to find 5? 5, 4, or 1?
pic: list = [8, 1, 6, 2, 5]\nsearch for 5, starting at item 1

key: COMP.PROG.L08.02|Look at the list. What is the list after one pass? 2, 4, 5; 5, 2, 4; or 4, 2, 5?
pic: list = [5, 2, 4]\none pass: compare each pair, swap if left is bigger

key: COMP.PROG.L08.02|Look at the list. The search looks for 4. What happens? It checks all 3 and does not find it, it finds it at the first item, or it stops at item 2 and gives up?
pic: list = [6, 2, 7]\nsearch for 4, starting at item 1

key: COMP.PROG.L08.02|A list of 100 names is sorted A to Z. Why is that helpful? You can find a name faster, the list gets much shorter, or the names change their spelling?
COMP.PROG.L08.02|Put the steps of linear search in order. The cards say: Stop if it matches., Check the first item., Move to the next item if not.
COMP.PROG.L08.02|Shmuli lines up the boys in his class by height for a picture, shortest to tallest. What is he doing? Sorting, searching, or deleting?
COMP.PROG.L08.02|Look at the list. What is the list after one pass? 3, 1, 8; 1, 3, 8; or 8, 3, 1?
pic: list = [3, 8, 1]\none pass: compare each pair, swap if left is bigger

key: COMP.PROG.L08.02|What does linear search do? Checks items one at a time, sorts the whole list first, or guesses one random item?
COMP.PROG.L08.02|Which list is sorted smallest to largest? 2, 5, 9; 9, 5, 2; or 5, 2, 9?
COMP.PROG.L08.02|In the coat idea, how do you search? One hook at a time, or all hooks at once?
how: A new way: linear search is like looking for your coat on a row of hooks, checking each hook from the door until you find yours.

key: COMP.PROG.L08.02|Sort 8 and 3 smallest first. Which comes first? 3, or 8?
how: A simpler step: sort just two numbers. The smaller one goes first.

key: COMP.PROG.L08.02|A list holds 7, 3 and 9, in that order. What is item 2? 3, or 7?
how: The skill underneath: Lists (Computing Level 6). Searching and sorting both work on a list, item by item.

key: COMP.DIG.L08.02|What does a filter do to rows that do not match? Hides them, deletes them forever, or colors them red?
how: Big tables are hard to read. Sort puts the rows in order by one column, like largest to smallest. Filter hides rows you do not need, like showing only grade 2. The hidden rows are still there, just out of sight. With sort and filter, you find answers in seconds!

key: COMP.DIG.L08.02|Look at the sheet. Sorted by Minutes, largest first, who is at the top? Eli, Dovid, or Moshe?
how: Sorting by Minutes, largest first, puts the biggest number at the top.
